subject: Post-call: integration recap & constrained-decoding / validation plan

Cc: product@finexa.com
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: integration scope and next steps

Neha / team — thanks for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Goal: wire Finexa's customer assistant to Redwood for conversational answers + a reranker/embedding index for private docs.
- Must-haves: predictable 99th pct latency < 350ms for short queries, JSON-constrained responses for tool invocation, RBAC-friendly auth, and audit logs for compliance.
- Primary integration points: SDK-based client in our backend, service-to-service auth (token-based), and an edge routing policy to prefer a lower-latency model for recall queries.

Next steps we discussed:
1) Finexa: share a short sample corpus + current embedding index metrics (ETA Mon 12/06)
2) Redwood: provide a checklist and a preliminary JSON schema for constrained decoding + suggested retry patterns
3) Schedule a 30-min technical onboarding for the devs (ideally Wed or Thu)

Attachments: I uploaded a short list of our compliance questions to the shared drive (link in the notes).

Thanks — James
Product Manager | Finexa

- Auth patterns: short-lived signed tokens + optional mTLS for Private deployments
- Routing recommendations: latency-first policy for short queries, cost-aware fallback to quantized variants for bulk rerank jobs
- Structured output reliability: constrained decoding + validator hook (server-side) + retry/backoff pattern when validation fails

Immediate asks for Finexa so we can prepare a tight plan:
- Share a small example of the query distribution (p50/p95 length) and an example doc you will index
- Confirm whether you'd prefer token-auth or a managed OIDC flow for the initial pilot

I've looped Dev (solutions eng) and Marissa (CS) to own the technical onboarding. Proposed times: Wed 12/08 10:00am PT or Thu 12/09 11:30am PT. Which works best?

Best,
Neha Kapoor

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@finexa.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: integration scope and next steps — technical notes

James — adding a few concrete patterns so your engineers can validate feasibility before the call:

1) SDK / Auth
- SDKs: Node v18+ and Python 3.10+ supported. We'll provide config snippets for consistent retry/backoff and a validation hook that runs after decode.
- Auth: for pilot we recommend short-lived asymmetric tokens (issued by your auth system, signed by your Key ID). We'll include an example middleware for token rotation. If you want OIDC, we can map roles from your IdP to Redwood policies.

2) Routing / Model variants
- Routing policy: implement a two-tier route: "low-latency" model (smaller fp16) for conversational short responses; fallback to "high-accuracy" variant for multi-step tool calls or low-confidence outputs. Routing is policy-driven and configured at the API route level.

3) Structured output validation + constrained decoding
- Constrained decoding: we suggest two layers — (A) model-level constraints (format tokens / exemplar priming) and (B) server-side validator that enforces the JSON schema.
- Validation pattern: run validator synchronously after decode; if schema fails, attempt up to 2 automatic regeneration attempts with increasing temperature control (0.0 -> 0.2) and prefix hints, then surface detailed failure to your app. This keeps latency bounded while improving recovery.
- Retry/backoff: per-request: immediate second attempt (low-temp), then 200ms backoff and final attempt with stronger schema priming. Count these in observability so you can track regeneration rate.

4) Embeddings / Reranker guidance
- For private docs: we recommend sharded embedding indexes (per-tenant) and periodic reembedding for changed docs. For rerankers, run a small CPU-based candidate scoring step before hitting the model for rerank to limit token costs.

I attached a tiny sample validator snippet and the schema file (constrained-json-schema-v1.json). We'll bring runnable examples to the onboarding.

— Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
